published_games.title: FOUNDRY — A Question of Severance
published_games.one_line: Turn-based roguelike (Canvas2D tiles) where you play a robot, a 'unit' of the sealed Vindhall Works factory 19 years after S.U.R.T. severed the staff; pick kit/condition, seed, optional Ironman; has a free/paid edition split (data2.js, sprites2.js).
published_games.controls: Keyboard-first: arrows / hjkl / yubn / numpad to move+bump; . or z wait, s search, m map, i inventory, g/, pick up, f fire/cast, r, p, x examine, c close door, < > stairs, Enter, Esc menu/skip opening, ? How to Play, Shift+M mute; mouse hover tooltips, click buttons and minimap. No touch handlers.
published_games.repo: unknown (not determinable: no GitHub access; Vercel project not reachable)
published_games.framework: none/static: plain HTML + 15 JS files (no bundler), CSS, Canvas2D with procedurally painted sprites, no image assets
published_games.last_deploy: unknown (no Vercel record). Response last-modified equals request time (served fresh), not informative.
published_games.total_bytes_approx: ~2.2 MB JS+CSS uncompressed (js 2.2MB: data.js 449k, rules 406k, ui 400k, sprites 304k, data2 193k, render 134k, mapgen 111k, sprites2 105k, model 99k, ai 66k, save/sound/util/main ~27k; css 54k; html 7.6k)

mobile.notes: document.documentElement.scrollWidth==390 only because body has overflow:hidden; the title screen's 'Your Unit' setup column overflows to x=413 and #titleScreen scrollWidth=508, so the 'FOUNDRY' title and setup form are clipped with no way to scroll. CSS has no width @media queries (only prefers-reduced-motion), no touch/pointer handlers anywhere. A tap on POWER ON does start the game and renders the opening at 390 wide, but gameplay is keyboard-only (Esc skips opening; movement keys) so effectively unplayable on phone.

framing.notes: No X-Frame-Options or CSP headers on / or /js/*; only access-control-allow-origin:* . Iframe from http://localhost:8080 rendered with title screen present (#btnNew found inside frame), 0 console messages. Embedding inside michaelking.systems is blocked only by michaelking.systems's own header policy (frame-src falls back to default-src 'self' and would block this origin) - that is the portfolio's CSP, not the game's.
